name: Meenakshi Sundareswarar Temple
description: Historic Dravidian masterpiece featuring 14 towering Gopurams, Golden Lotus Tank, and Thousand Pillar Hall.
fullStory: Built over 2,500 years ago and expanded by Nayak Rulers in the 16th-17th centuries, the Meenakshi Temple is the beating heart of Madurai. It boasts 14 magnificent gopurams (gateway towers), the largest standing at 170 feet. Inside lies the Ashta Shakthi Mandapam, Meenakshi Nayakkar Mandapam, Thousand Pillar Museum housing ancient bronze idols, and the sacred Potramarai Kulam (Golden Lotus Pond).
dressCode: Traditional Indian attire required (Shoulders & knees covered. Mobile phones restricted inside inner sanctum).
bestTimeToVisit: Early morning 6:00 AM or evening 7:00 PM during Night Aarti
address: East Chitrai Street, Main Town, Madurai 625001

name: Thirumalai Nayakkar Mahal
description: 17th-century grand palace featuring massive 82-foot white pillars, celestial pavilion, and light & sound show.
fullStory: Constructed in 1636 AD by King Thirumalai Nayak with assistance from an Italian architect, this palace is a classic fusion of Dravidian and European Islamic architectural styles. The central courtyard (Swarga Vilasam) covers 41,000 sq ft and is held by colossal stucco-plastered pillars.
bestTimeToVisit: 3:30 PM for palace photography followed by Sound & Light show

name: Vandiyur Mariamman Teppakulam
description: Massive 16-acre temple tank built in 1645 AD featuring an island mandapam called Maiya Mandapam.
fullStory: Excavated when brick soil was dug to construct Thirumalai Nayakkar Palace, this tank was converted into a sacred reservoir fed by Vaigai river channels. It hosts the colorful Float Festival (Teppothsavam) in January/February where illuminated floats carry temple deities across the water.
timings: Open 24 Hours (Best at Sunset / Illuminated evening)
bestTimeToVisit: 5:30 PM to 7:00 PM for sunset reflection on water

name: Koodal Azhagar Temple
description: Ancient 108 Divya Desam Vishnu temple showcasing Lord Vishnu in 3 postures (Sitting, Standing, Reclining).
fullStory: One of the oldest temples in South India, Koodal Azhagar Temple features a unique three-tiered vimanam. On the ground floor Lord Vishnu is in sitting posture (Koodal Azhagar), second floor in standing posture (Sri Surya Narayana), and third floor in reclining posture (Sri Ranganatha).
address: Near Periyar Bus Stand, Koodal Alagar Perumal Koil St, Madurai 625001

name: Gandhi Memorial Museum
description: Housed in Rani Mangammal's 17th-century summer palace, displaying Gandhi's blood-stained garment and freedom struggle relics.
fullStory: Established in 1959, this is one of five Gandhi Sanghralayas in India. It preserves Mahatma Gandhi's original blood-stained garment from his 1948 assassination in New Delhi, along with over 100 rare original photographs, letters, and the history of India's freedom struggle.

name: Alagar Kovil (Kallazhagar Temple)
description: Picturesque Lord Vishnu temple situated at the foot of Solaimalai hills surrounded by dense green forest.
fullStory: Located 21 km northeast of Madurai at the foot of Solaimalai hill, this temple is dedicated to Lord Kallazhagar (Vishnu). During the grand Chithirai Festival, Lord Azhagar travels on a golden horse to Madurai to enter the Vaigai River. Higher up the hill lies Pazhamudircholai Murugan Temple and Nubura Gangai holy spring.
bestTimeToVisit: 7:00 AM morning for fresh mountain air

name: Samanar Hills (Keelakuyilkudi)
description: Ancient 1st-century BCE Jain rock-cut caves with Tirthankara relief sculptures and panoramic sunset views.
fullStory: Samanar Malai is a rocky hillock in Keelakuyilkudi village where Jain monks lived 2,000 years ago. The caves feature carved bas-relief images of Jain Tirthankaras like Parsvanatha and Mahavira, ancient Tamil-Brahmi inscriptions, and a hilltop lotus pond (Pechipallam).

name: Thiruparankundram Murugan Temple
description: One of the 6 sacred abodes (Arupadai Veedu) of Lord Murugan, carved directly into a monolithic granite rock hill.
fullStory: Built in 6th century AD by Pandyan Rulers, this rock-cut temple is where Lord Murugan married Deivanai (daughter of Lord Indra) after defeating demon Surapadman. The sanctum sanctorum is carved directly into the living granite rock.
